title: Docker
level: containers basics → Dockerfile mastery → security & production on ECS

sections.title: Mental model: what a container really is
sections.intro_md:
**A container is just a normal Linux process with isolation and limits** — not a mini-VM.

```
 ┌──────────────────────── Virtual machines ───────────────────┐   ┌──────────────────────── Containers ─────────────────────────┐
 │  App A      App B                                          │   │  App A        App B        App C                            │
 │  Libs       Libs                                           │   │  Libs         Libs         Libs     ← image layers           │
 │  Guest OS   Guest OS   ← full kernel each (GBs, slow boot)  │   │ ───────────── container runtime (containerd/runc) ─────────  │
 │ ───────── Hypervisor ─────────                              │   │  Host OS kernel  ← SHARED (MBs, starts in ms)                │
 │  Hardware                                                   │   │  Hardware                                                    │
 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Linux features that make a container:
- **Namespaces** — what the process can *see*: own PID tree, network stack, mount points, hostname, users.
- **cgroups** — what it can *use*: CPU, memory, I/O limits.
- **Union filesystem (overlayfs)** — image layers stacked read-only + one thin writable layer.
- **Capabilities, seccomp, AppArmor/SELinux** — what it's *allowed to do* (syscalls, privileges).

**Docker architecture:**
```flow
sequence: What actually runs when you type docker run
actors: docker CLI, dockerd, containerd, runc, Registry
docker CLI -> dockerd: REST API: run nginx
dockerd -> Registry: pull image (if missing)
Registry --> dockerd: layers
dockerd -> containerd: create container
containerd -> runc: start process
> runc sets up namespaces (isolation) and cgroups (limits), then starts your process. A container is just an isolated Linux process.
runc --> docker CLI: container running
```

**Image → container lifecycle:**
```flow
pipeline: Image to container lifecycle
Dockerfile > Instructions, each creating a layer.
build > Produces an image: read-only layers with an ID/digest.
push → registry > ECR, Docker Hub or the GitLab registry.
run > Container = image layers + a thin writable layer + a process + config.
created → running → stopped > Stopping keeps the writable layer.
removed > The writable layer is deleted. Anything not in a volume is lost.
```

questions.title: Container vs VM
questions.short_md: A VM virtualises **hardware** and runs a full guest OS kernel; a container virtualises the **OS** — processes share the host kernel, isolated by namespaces and limited by cgroups. Containers are lighter and start faster; VMs give stronger isolation. (Fargate/AgentCore/Lambda add microVM isolation underneath containers for multi-tenant safety.)
questions.body_md: **Short answer:** A VM virtualises **hardware** and runs a full guest OS kernel; a container virtualises the **OS** — processes share the host kernel, isolated by namespaces and limited by cgroups. Containers are lighter and start faster; VMs give stronger isolation. (Fargate/AgentCore/Lambda add microVM isolation underneath containers for multi-tenant safety.)

questions.title: Image vs container
questions.short_md: An **image** is an immutable template (layers + metadata: entrypoint, env, user). A **container** is a running (or stopped) instance of an image with its own writable layer. Many containers can run from one image.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** An **image** is an immutable template (layers + metadata: entrypoint, env, user). A **container** is a running (or stopped) instance of an image with its own writable layer. Many containers can run from one image.

```bash
docker build -t api:1.4.0 .
docker run -d --name api1 -p 8000:8000 api:1.4.0
docker run -d --name api2 -p 8001:8000 api:1.4.0     # same image, separate container
docker ps; docker logs -f api1; docker exec -it api1 sh; docker stop api1; docker rm api1
```

questions.title: Registries, repositories, tags and digests
questions.short_md: A registry stores images (`123456789012.dkr.ecr.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/api`). A **tag** (`:1.4.0`, `:latest`) is a **movable** label. A **digest** (`@sha256:ab12…`) is the content hash — **immutable**. Deploy by digest (or immutable tags) so "what's running" is unambiguous.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** A registry stores images (`123456789012.dkr.ecr.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/api`). A **tag** (`:1.4.0`, `:latest`) is a **movable** label. A **digest** (`@sha256:ab12…`) is the content hash — **immutable**. Deploy by digest (or immutable tags) so "what's running" is unambiguous.

```bash
aws ecr get-login-password | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin $ECR
docker tag api:1.4.0 $ECR/api:git-3f9c2ab
docker push $ECR/api:git-3f9c2ab        # prints digest sha256:...
```
**ECR features:** private repos, IAM auth, **tag immutability**, image scanning (basic / enhanced with Inspector), lifecycle policies (delete old images), replication, pull-through cache.

questions.title: `.dockerignore`
questions.short_md: Excludes files from the **build context** sent to the builder → faster builds, smaller images, no secrets leaking into layers, better cache hits.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** Excludes files from the **build context** sent to the builder → faster builds, smaller images, no secrets leaking into layers, better cache hits.

```
.git
.venv
node_modules
__pycache__/
*.pyc
.env
tests/
dist/
```

questions.title: Image layers and build cache
questions.short_md: Each filesystem-changing instruction (`RUN`, `COPY`, `ADD`) creates a layer. Docker reuses a cached layer if the instruction **and its inputs** are unchanged; once a layer changes, **all later layers rebuild**. So: put rarely-changing steps first (install dependencies), frequently-changing steps last (copy source).
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** Each filesystem-changing instruction (`RUN`, `COPY`, `ADD`) creates a layer. Docker reuses a cached layer if the instruction **and its inputs** are unchanged; once a layer changes, **all later layers rebuild**. So: put rarely-changing steps first (install dependencies), frequently-changing steps last (copy source).

```dockerfile
# ❌ any code change reinstalls all dependencies
COPY . .
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt

# ✅ dependencies cached until requirements change
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
```
**Pitfall:** deleting files in a later layer doesn't shrink the image — the earlier layer still contains them. Clean up **in the same `RUN`**.

questions.title: Ports: `EXPOSE` vs publishing
questions.short_md: `EXPOSE 8000` is **documentation/metadata** only. `-p 8080:8000` actually **publishes** host port 8080 → container port 8000. In ECS/awsvpc you set `containerPort` in the task definition; the ENI gets the port directly.

questions.title: `CMD` vs `ENTRYPOINT`, exec vs shell form
questions.short_md: `ENTRYPOINT` defines the program; `CMD` provides default args that `docker run img <args>` replaces. **Exec form** (`["uvicorn", "app:app"]`) runs the process directly as PID 1 and receives signals. **Shell form** (`uvicorn app:app`) wraps it in `/bin/sh -c` → the shell is PID 1 and may not forward `SIGTERM` → no graceful shutdown.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** `ENTRYPOINT` defines the program; `CMD` provides default args that `docker run img <args>` replaces. **Exec form** (`["uvicorn", "app:app"]`) runs the process directly as PID 1 and receives signals. **Shell form** (`uvicorn app:app`) wraps it in `/bin/sh -c` → the shell is PID 1 and may not forward `SIGTERM` → no graceful shutdown.

```dockerfile
ENTRYPOINT ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0"]
CMD ["--port", "8000"]
# docker run img --port 9000  → overrides CMD only
```

questions.title: `ARG` vs `ENV`
questions.short_md: `ARG` exists only during build (`--build-arg VERSION=1.4`), `ENV` persists into the running container. **Neither is for secrets** — both are visible in image history/metadata. Use BuildKit secret mounts for build secrets and Secrets Manager at runtime.

questions.title: Multi-stage builds
questions.short_md: Use one stage with compilers/build tools, then copy only the results into a small runtime stage → smaller image, fewer vulnerabilities, no build tools in production.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** Use one stage with compilers/build tools, then copy only the results into a small runtime stage → smaller image, fewer vulnerabilities, no build tools in production.

```dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
FROM python:3.13-slim AS builder
COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.8 /uv /bin/uv
WORKDIR /app
COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-install-project      # deps only → cached layer
COPY src/ ./src/
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv uv sync --frozen --no-dev

FROM python:3.13-slim AS runtime
RUN useradd --create-home --uid 10001 appuser
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=builder --chown=appuser:appuser /app /app
ENV PATH="/app/.venv/bin:$PATH" PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
USER 10001
EXPOSE 8000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s CMD python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8000/health')"
ENTRYPOINT ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
```
Frontend example: `node` stage runs `vite build` → `nginx:alpine` stage copies `dist/`.

questions.title: BuildKit features: cache mounts, secret mounts, multi-platform
questions.short_md: RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip pip install -r requirements.txt   # persistent pip cache RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npmrc,target=/root/.npmrc npm ci                       # secret NOT stored in layer
questions.body_md:
```dockerfile
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip pip install -r requirements.txt   # persistent pip cache
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npmrc,target=/root/.npmrc npm ci                       # secret NOT stored in layer
```
```bash
docker build --secret id=npmrc,src=$HOME/.npmrc .
docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 -t $IMG --push .   # multi-arch
```
**ARM64 matters on AWS:** Graviton (ECS/Lambda) is cheaper; AgentCore Runtime requires ARM64. Building on an x86 laptop needs `--platform linux/arm64` (QEMU emulation or native ARM builders).

questions.title: Choosing a base image
questions.short_md: Pin versions (`python:3.13.7-slim-bookworm` or `@sha256:`), rebuild regularly for patches.
questions.body_md:
| Base | Size | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `python:3.13` | large | has compilers; for builder stage |
| `python:3.13-slim` | medium | Debian minimal; good default |
| `python:3.13-alpine` | small | musl libc → many Python wheels must compile; sometimes slower/buggy |
| distroless / Chainguard / Docker Hardened Images | very small | no shell/package manager → fewer CVEs; debugging harder |
| `scratch` | empty | static binaries (Go) |

Pin versions (`python:3.13.7-slim-bookworm` or `@sha256:`), rebuild regularly for patches.

questions.title: Reducing image size and vulnerabilities
questions.short_md: Multi-stage, slim/distroless base, `--no-install-recommends` and clean apt lists in the same `RUN`, no dev dependencies, `.dockerignore`, remove build tools, scan and fix, pin + rebuild weekly.
questions.body_md:
Multi-stage, slim/distroless base, `--no-install-recommends` and clean apt lists in the same `RUN`, no dev dependencies, `.dockerignore`, remove build tools, scan and fix, pin + rebuild weekly.

```dockerfile
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libpq5 \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
```

questions.title: Running as non-root
questions.short_md: By default containers run as root (UID 0). If an attacker escapes the app, root in the container makes escalation easier. Create a user, `USER 10001`, own only needed files, and in ECS also set `readonlyRootFilesystem` and drop capabilities.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** By default containers run as root (UID 0). If an attacker escapes the app, root in the container makes escalation easier. Create a user, `USER 10001`, own only needed files, and in ECS also set `readonlyRootFilesystem` and drop capabilities.

**Pitfall:** non-root can't bind ports < 1024 — use 8000/8080.

questions.title: Reproducible builds
questions.short_md: Pin base image digests, lockfiles (`uv.lock`, `package-lock.json`), pinned tool versions, `--frozen`/`npm ci`, no `apt-get upgrade` of unpinned packages in app images (rebuild base instead), build in CI not laptops.
questions.body_md: Pin base image digests, lockfiles (`uv.lock`, `package-lock.json`), pinned tool versions, `--frozen`/`npm ci`, no `apt-get upgrade` of unpinned packages in app images (rebuild base instead), build in CI not laptops.

questions.short_md: LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="https://gitlab.example.com/payments/api" \ org.opencontainers.image.revision="$GIT_SHA"

questions.title: Docker networking modes
questions.short_md: docker network create app-net docker run -d --network app-net --name db postgres:16 docker run -d --network app-net -e DB_HOST=db api:1.4     # "db" resolves via Docker DNS
questions.body_md:
| Mode | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `bridge` (default) | private network on host; containers reach each other by **name** on user-defined bridges; publish ports to reach from host |
| `host` | shares host network stack (no isolation, no port mapping) |
| `none` | no networking |
| `overlay` | multi-host (Swarm) |
| **ECS `awsvpc`** | each task gets its **own ENI** and private IP in your VPC; security groups per task |

```bash
docker network create app-net
docker run -d --network app-net --name db postgres:16
docker run -d --network app-net -e DB_HOST=db api:1.4     # "db" resolves via Docker DNS
```

questions.title: Volumes vs bind mounts vs tmpfs
questions.short_md: In production on ECS/Fargate: containers are **ephemeral**; persist data in RDS/DynamoDB/S3 or EFS volumes, not container disk.
questions.body_md:
| | Volume | Bind mount | tmpfs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Managed by | Docker (`docker volume`) | you (host path) | memory |
| Use | persistent data (DB in dev) | live-reload source code in dev | temp secrets/scratch |
| Portability | good | host-dependent | — |

In production on ECS/Fargate: containers are **ephemeral**; persist data in RDS/DynamoDB/S3 or EFS volumes, not container disk.

questions.title: Docker Compose for local development
questions.short_md: services: api: build: . ports: ["8000:8000"] env_file: .env.local depends_on: db: { condition: service_healthy } develop: watch: - { action: sync, path: ./src, target: /app/src }   # compose watch: live sync db: image: postgres:16 environment: { POSTGRES_PASSWORD: dev } healthcheck: { test: ["CMD", "pg_isready"], interval: 5s } volumes: [pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data] volumes: { pgdata: {} }
questions.body_md:
```yaml
# compose.yaml
services:
  api:
    build: .
    ports: ["8000:8000"]
    env_file: .env.local
    depends_on:
      db: { condition: service_healthy }
    develop:
      watch:
        - { action: sync, path: ./src, target: /app/src }   # compose watch: live sync
  db:
    image: postgres:16
    environment: { POSTGRES_PASSWORD: dev }
    healthcheck: { test: ["CMD", "pg_isready"], interval: 5s }
    volumes: [pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data]
volumes: { pgdata: {} }
```
`docker compose up -d`, `docker compose logs -f api`, `docker compose down -v`.

questions.title: Local vs production configuration (12-factor)
questions.short_md: Same image everywhere; configuration via **environment variables** and secrets injected at runtime (ECS task definition `secrets` from Secrets Manager/SSM). Don't bake environment-specific config or secrets into images. Log to **stdout/stderr** (collected by awslogs/FireLens).

questions.title: Containers are ephemeral — implications
questions.short_md: Anything written to the container filesystem disappears when the task is replaced. Store state externally; design for being killed at any time (graceful shutdown, idempotent work, retries).
questions.body_md: Anything written to the container filesystem disappears when the task is replaced. Store state externally; design for being killed at any time (graceful shutdown, idempotent work, retries).

questions.title: SIGTERM and graceful shutdown
questions.short_md: `docker stop` / ECS sends **SIGTERM** to PID 1, waits a grace period (Docker default 10 s; ECS `stopTimeout` default 30 s, max 120 s on Fargate), then **SIGKILL**. Your app must catch SIGTERM: stop accepting new work, finish in-flight requests, close connections, exit.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** `docker stop` / ECS sends **SIGTERM** to PID 1, waits a grace period (Docker default 10 s; ECS `stopTimeout` default 30 s, max 120 s on Fargate), then **SIGKILL**. Your app must catch SIGTERM: stop accepting new work, finish in-flight requests, close connections, exit.

```flow
pipeline: Graceful shutdown on ECS
Deploy / scale-in > ECS decides to stop a task.
Deregister from ALB > No new requests; in-flight ones continue during the deregistration delay.
SIGTERM > Sent to PID 1 in the container. Your app must handle it (exec form CMD, or an init like tini).
App drains > Stop accepting work, finish in-flight requests, close connections, flush logs.
SIGKILL after stopTimeout > Anything still running is killed hard.
```
Requirements: exec-form `ENTRYPOINT` (app is PID 1) or an init (`tini`, `docker run --init`, ECS `initProcessEnabled`) that forwards signals and reaps zombies. Uvicorn/Gunicorn handle SIGTERM gracefully.

```python
import signal, asyncio
stop = asyncio.Event()
signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, lambda *_: stop.set())   # worker loop checks stop.is_set()
```

questions.title: Docker `HEALTHCHECK` vs ECS vs ALB health checks
questions.short_md: Keep `/health` cheap (liveness); a separate readiness check can test dependencies. Use `startPeriod` / health-check grace period for slow starts. (ECS ignores the Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK — define it in the task definition.)
questions.body_md:
| Check | Who runs it | Effect if failing |
|---|---|---|
| Dockerfile `HEALTHCHECK` | Docker engine | marks container unhealthy (Docker itself doesn't restart it) |
| ECS container `healthCheck` (task definition) | ECS agent, inside the container | ECS replaces the task (essential container) |
| ALB target group health check | load balancer → HTTP path | stops routing traffic; ECS replaces unhealthy targets |

Keep `/health` cheap (liveness); a separate readiness check can test dependencies. Use `startPeriod` / health-check grace period for slow starts. (ECS ignores the Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK — define it in the task definition.)

questions.title: Resource limits (CPU, memory)
questions.short_md: docker run --memory=512m --cpus=1.0 api:1.4
questions.body_md:
```bash
docker run --memory=512m --cpus=1.0 api:1.4
```
Exceeding memory → process **OOM-killed** (exit code **137**, `OOMKilled: true`). CPU limit → throttling (slower), not a kill. In ECS: task-level CPU/memory (Fargate) plus container `memory` (hard) / `memoryReservation` (soft). Python services: set worker counts based on memory, watch for leaks.

questions.title: Exit codes you should recognise
questions.short_md: "exec format error" = image built for a different CPU architecture (amd64 vs arm64).
questions.body_md:
| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | clean exit (for a web server, unexpected — something told it to stop) |
| 1 | application error (check logs) |
| 126 / 127 | command not executable / not found (bad ENTRYPOINT, missing binary, wrong arch) |
| 137 | SIGKILL — OOM or killed after stop timeout |
| 139 | segfault (native lib, wrong architecture) |
| 143 | SIGTERM received and exited |

"exec format error" = image built for a different CPU architecture (amd64 vs arm64).

questions.title: Container security layers
questions.short_md: Build:   minimal pinned base → no secrets in layers → scan (Trivy/Inspector) → SBOM → sign (Cosign) Registry: private ECR, tag immutability, scan on push, lifecycle policy, only CI can push Deploy:  verify signature/digest, least-privilege task role, secrets from Secrets Manager Runtime: non-root, read-only root FS, drop Linux capabilities, no privileged mode, no docker.sock mounts, seccomp default, resource limits, private subnets + SGs, GuardDuty runtime monitoring
questions.body_md:
```
 Build:   minimal pinned base → no secrets in layers → scan (Trivy/Inspector) → SBOM → sign (Cosign)
 Registry: private ECR, tag immutability, scan on push, lifecycle policy, only CI can push
 Deploy:  verify signature/digest, least-privilege task role, secrets from Secrets Manager
 Runtime: non-root, read-only root FS, drop Linux capabilities, no privileged mode,
          no docker.sock mounts, seccomp default, resource limits, private subnets + SGs,
          GuardDuty runtime monitoring
```

questions.title: Why never mount `/var/run/docker.sock` or use `--privileged`?
questions.short_md: The Docker socket gives **root on the host** (start any container with host mounts). `--privileged` disables most isolation. Both turn a container compromise into a host compromise.
questions.body_md: The Docker socket gives **root on the host** (start any container with host mounts). `--privileged` disables most isolation. Both turn a container compromise into a host compromise.

questions.title: Secrets: what not to do
questions.short_md: ❌ `ENV API_KEY=...`, ❌ `COPY .env`, ❌ `ARG TOKEN` used in `RUN` (visible in history), ❌ secrets in image labels. ✅ BuildKit `--mount=type=secret` for build time; ✅ ECS `secrets` (Secrets Manager/SSM) or fetch at startup via the task role for runtime.
questions.body_md: ❌ `ENV API_KEY=...`, ❌ `COPY .env`, ❌ `ARG TOKEN` used in `RUN` (visible in history), ❌ secrets in image labels. ✅ BuildKit `--mount=type=secret` for build time; ✅ ECS `secrets` (Secrets Manager/SSM) or fetch at startup via the task role for runtime.

questions.title: SBOM, scanning and signing
questions.short_md: - **SBOM** (Software Bill of Materials, SPDX/CycloneDX via Syft or `docker buildx --sbom`): lists every package → answer "are we affected by CVE-X?" quickly. - **Scanning** (Trivy, Grype, ECR enhanced scanning/Inspector): finds known CVEs; gate CI on critical/high with fix available. - **Signing** (Cosign/Sigstore, AWS Signer for ECR): proves the image came from your pipeline; verify before deploy. - **Provenance** (SLSA attestations): how/where it was built.
questions.body_md:
- **SBOM** (Software Bill of Materials, SPDX/CycloneDX via Syft or `docker buildx --sbom`): lists every package → answer "are we affected by CVE-X?" quickly.
- **Scanning** (Trivy, Grype, ECR enhanced scanning/Inspector): finds known CVEs; gate CI on critical/high with fix available.
- **Signing** (Cosign/Sigstore, AWS Signer for ECR): proves the image came from your pipeline; verify before deploy.
- **Provenance** (SLSA attestations): how/where it was built.

questions.title: Image tags: why not `latest`?
questions.short_md: `latest` is just a mutable default tag — you can't tell what's running, rollbacks are ambiguous, and nodes may cache different versions. Use commit-SHA tags + digests; enable ECR tag immutability.
questions.body_md: `latest` is just a mutable default tag — you can't tell what's running, rollbacks are ambiguous, and nodes may cache different versions. Use commit-SHA tags + digests; enable ECR tag immutability.

questions.title: Offline-friendly / air-gapped secure image
questions.short_md: Mirror base images and packages into an internal registry/artifact repository (ECR pull-through cache, CodeArtifact), pin digests, vendor wheels, build with no internet (`--network=none` for steps), scan and sign internally.

questions.title: Container crash-loops. How do you debug?
questions.short_md: pipeline: Debugging a crash-looping container Read the logs > `docker logs` / CloudWatch: is there an error at startup? Inspect exit state > `docker inspect` → `State.ExitCode`, `OOMKilled`. Decode the exit code > 137 → killed (often memory); 127 → command not found; "exec format error" → wrong CPU architecture. Run it interactively > `docker run --rm -it --entrypoint sh img`, then start the app by hand. Check the environment > Env vars and secrets present? Config paths? Permissions (can non-root write to /app)? Dependencies reachable (DB DNS)?
questions.body_md:
```flow
pipeline: Debugging a crash-looping container
Read the logs > `docker logs` / CloudWatch: is there an error at startup?
Inspect exit state > `docker inspect` → `State.ExitCode`, `OOMKilled`.
Decode the exit code > 137 → killed (often memory); 127 → command not found; "exec format error" → wrong CPU architecture.
Run it interactively > `docker run --rm -it --entrypoint sh img`, then start the app by hand.
Check the environment > Env vars and secrets present? Config paths? Permissions (can non-root write to /app)? Dependencies reachable (DB DNS)?
```

questions.title: Works locally but ECS can't pull the image (`CannotPullContainerError`)
questions.short_md: - **Network:** task in private subnet with no NAT and no **VPC endpoints** for ECR (`ecr.api`, `ecr.dkr`) + **S3 gateway endpoint** (layers are stored in S3) + CloudWatch Logs endpoint. - **Permissions:** task **execution role** lacks `ecr:GetAuthorizationToken`, `ecr:BatchGetImage`, `ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer` (use `AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy`). - **Image reference:** wrong tag/digest/region/account; repository policy for cross-account. - **Architecture:** ARM image on X86 task (or vice versa) → task fails after pull.
questions.body_md:
- **Network:** task in private subnet with no NAT and no **VPC endpoints** for ECR (`ecr.api`, `ecr.dkr`) + **S3 gateway endpoint** (layers are stored in S3) + CloudWatch Logs endpoint.
- **Permissions:** task **execution role** lacks `ecr:GetAuthorizationToken`, `ecr:BatchGetImage`, `ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer` (use `AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy`).
- **Image reference:** wrong tag/digest/region/account; repository policy for cross-account.
- **Architecture:** ARM image on X86 task (or vice versa) → task fails after pull.

questions.title: ECS task stops after ~30 s with "unhealthy"
questions.short_md: App binds `127.0.0.1` instead of `0.0.0.0`; wrong port; health-check path returns 404/redirect; app slower to start than grace period/`startPeriod`; health check command missing in image (`curl` not installed in slim/distroless); security group blocks ALB → task port; dependency failure making `/health` fail.
questions.body_md: App binds `127.0.0.1` instead of `0.0.0.0`; wrong port; health-check path returns 404/redirect; app slower to start than grace period/`startPeriod`; health check command missing in image (`curl` not installed in slim/distroless); security group blocks ALB → task port; dependency failure making `/health` fail.

questions.title: Build is slow in CI
questions.short_md: No layer cache between runners → use registry cache (`--cache-from/--cache-to type=registry`), order instructions for cache, cache mounts for package managers, smaller build context (`.dockerignore`), native ARM builders instead of emulation.
questions.body_md: No layer cache between runners → use registry cache (`--cache-from/--cache-to type=registry`), order instructions for cache, cache mounts for package managers, smaller build context (`.dockerignore`), native ARM builders instead of emulation.

questions.title: Image is 2.5 GB
questions.short_md: `docker history` to see which layers are large → compilers and dev deps (multi-stage), CUDA/torch where not needed (CPU wheels), caches left in layers (clean in same RUN or cache mounts), copying `.git`/data folders (`.dockerignore`).

questions.title: Container gets OOM-killed under load
questions.short_md: Measure per-worker memory; reduce workers or increase memory; fix leaks (unbounded caches); stream large files instead of loading; set Python `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX` for glibc fragmentation if needed; add memory alarms.

sections.title: Cheat sheet
sections.intro_md:
| Concept | One-liner |
|---|---|
| Container | process + namespaces + cgroups + layered FS |
| Image vs container | template vs running instance + writable layer |
| Tag vs digest | movable label vs immutable hash |
| Layers | cache until changed; order deps before source |
| Multi-stage | build tools in builder, small runtime |
| CMD vs ENTRYPOINT | args vs executable; use exec form |
| ARG vs ENV | build-time vs runtime; neither for secrets |
| BuildKit | cache mounts, secret mounts, multi-arch |
| Non-root | `USER 10001`, read-only FS, drop caps |
| SIGTERM | PID 1 must handle it; grace period then SIGKILL |
| Health | Docker vs ECS vs ALB checks differ |
| Exit 137 | OOM / SIGKILL; 127 bad command; exec format = arch |
| Networking | bridge DNS by name; ECS awsvpc = ENI per task |
| Supply chain | pin, scan, SBOM, sign, immutable ECR tags |
